title: The constructible hierarchy

based_on.title: Set Theory
based_on.pages: 86–87 (§20, definable subsets, Definition 20.2, Lemma 20.3 and Exercise 20.1); revision 2026-01-31

summary: Construct levels by definable subsets, prove their transitivity and ordinal bounds, and compare finite and countable domains with the full power-set construction.
abstract: Starting with the empty set, the constructible hierarchy keeps the subsets describable by a finite membership formula with finitely many parameters from the preceding level. At limit stages it takes unions. Truth over each set domain is defined by recursion on finite formulas, including the empty starting domain, so every successor step produces a well-defined set. The levels are transitive, increase with their index, and contain exactly the earlier ordinals while staying inside the corresponding rank stages. The finite levels agree with the rank hierarchy, but a countably infinite domain has only countably many definable subsets and uncountably many subsets altogether. Transitive models of ZF compute the same levels at the ordinal indices they contain. These construction facts prepare the separate proof that the full constructible class satisfies the set-theoretic axioms.
